newsitem.title: USA: Mexico refinancing plan blunts LDC debt losses.
newsitem.headline: Mexico refinancing plan blunts LDC debt losses.

text.p: Mexico's refinancing plans, unveiled on Tuesday, lifted the country's debt and helped limit losses among other emerging market issues, traders said.
"We're seeing a better buyside in Mexico. The rest of the market has seemed to widen and then stay still," one trader said.
Mexico revealed a plan to buy back $6.0 billion in floating rate notes due 2001 with proceeds from recent debt offerings.
Mexico discounts MXFLL19=RR climbed 1/2 to 93-1/2 bid, with their spread over comparable U.S. Treasuries tightening about 13 basis points.
Traders said much of the Mexico buying came early in the day on rumors of the restructuring, with only slight price gains after the actual news.

"The market opened fairly weak and started to sell off," said one trader. "If it hadn't been for the Mexico rumors hitting the tape and then Mexico actually doing something, we would probably be sitting 1/4 to 3/8 lower."
Elsewhere in Latin America, Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR were unchanged at 94-1/4, while Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR traded off 5/8 at 81 bid.
Traded volume remained thin in most issues, including Mexico, market experts said. They attributed the fairly slow trading to a prevalence of long positions.
"Customers have been very quiet now for a week or two," one trader said, adding that Bulgaria and Ecuador, more than other countries, saw selling on Tuesday.
Bulgaria FLRBs BGFLIRB=RR dipped 7/8 to 57-1/2, and Ecuador PDIs ECPDI=RR fell a percentage point to 68-1/8 bid.
Dollar-denominated Russian Vnesh loans RUVNUSLNS=RR fell 5/8 to 91-1/2.
Looking ahead, traders said they expected little additional boost from the Mexico refinancing news, but they agreed the move was positive for the country's economic outlook.
"Once the elections are done, I think progress Mexico has made in refinancing its debt efficiently opens it up for a ratings upgrade later this summer," a trader said.
